a OurBigBook.com
For pairwise coprime integers m1​,…,mr​, put M=∏i​mi​. The Chinese remainder theorem states that reduction gives an isomorphism
Z/MZ⟶∏i=1r​Z/mi​Z.
(1)
Equivalently, every system x≡ai​(modmi​) has one solution modulo M.
For existence, let Mi​=M/mi​. Since gcd(Mi​,mi​)=1, choose ui​ with ui​Mi​≡1(modmi​). Then
x=∑i=1r​ai​ui​Mi​
(2)
has every required residue: modulo mj​, all terms except the jth vanish and the remaining term is aj​. For uniqueness, if x and y have the same residues, every mi​ divides x−y. Pairwise coprimality then makes M divide x−y. Thus the simultaneous solution exists and is unique modulo M.

Choose distinct primes p1​,…,p1000​. The moduli pk2​ are pairwise coprime, so the Chinese remainder theorem supplies an integer N satisfying
N≡pk​−k(modpk2​)(1≤k≤1000).
(3)
Consequently
N+k≡pk​(modpk2​),
(4)
so pk​∣N+k but pk2​∤N+k. By the definition of a squarefull number, N+k is therefore not squarefull. Adding a sufficiently large multiple of ∏k​pk2​ makes N positive without changing any congruence. The integers N+1,…,N+1000 are the required consecutive integers.

2F (Topics in Analysis)

Words: 248 Articles: 1
Paper 1 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 248
2F OurBigBook.com
Sperner's lemma says that if a triangle is triangulated, its vertices are labelled 1,2,3, and label i is forbidden on the edge opposite vertex i, then an odd number of small triangles have all three labels.
To prove it, count incidences with edges whose endpoint labels are 1 and 2. Along the outer 12-edge, the labels begin at 1 and end at 2, so the number of 12 transitions is odd; no other boundary edge contributes. An interior edge contributes twice. A small triangle contributes an odd number precisely when its three labels are 1,2,3: a triangle using only 1,2 contributes two, and every other non-tricoloured triangle contributes zero. The number of tricoloured triangles is therefore odd.
Now suppose the closed sets Ai​ in the question existed. Let di​(x) be the distance from a point to a closed set Ai​. Empty triple intersection makes d1​+d2​+d3​>0, so
r(x)=d1​(x)+d2​(x)+d3​(x)d1​(x)v1​+d2​(x)v2​+d3​(x)v3​​
(5)
is a continuous function from the large triangle to itself, where vi​ is the vertex opposite αi​. Since the Ai​ cover the triangle, at least one di​(x) vanishes, so r(x) always lies on the boundary. On αi​⊆Ai​, its ith barycentric coordinate vanishes, hence r(αi​)⊆αi​. Thus r is face-preserving on the boundary; its boundary restriction is homotopic there to the identity by the straight-line homotopy. This would give a map from the triangle into its boundary whose boundary degree is one, contradicting the no-retraction theorem, the standard topological consequence of Sperner's lemma. Therefore the three closed sets must have a common point.

3H (Coding & Cryptography)

Words: 107 Articles: 1
Paper 1 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 107
3H OurBigBook.com
Let a memoryless source have probabilities p1​,…,pm​, and let a uniquely decodable D-ary code have word lengths ℓi​ and mean length L=∑i​pi​ℓi​. The Shannon source coding theorem states
HD​(p)≤L,HD​(p)=−∑i​pi​logD​pi​,
(6)
and that some prefix code satisfies
HD​(p)≤L<HD​(p)+1.
(7)
For the lower bound, the Kraft inequality gives K=∑i​D−ℓi​≤1. Set qi​=D−ℓi​/K. The Gibbs inequality, or nonnegativity of relative entropy, gives
0≤∑i​pi​logD​qi​pi​​=−HD​(p)+L+logD​K.
(8)
Therefore L≥HD​(p)−logD​K≥HD​(p).
For achievability choose ℓi​=⌈−logD​pi​⌉. Then ∑i​D−ℓi​≤∑i​pi​=1, so the converse part of the Kraft theorem supplies a prefix code with these lengths, and
L<∑i​pi​(−logD​pi​+1)=HD​(p)+1.
(9)
Hence the entropy is the optimal mean code length up to less than one code symbol.

This language is not context-free. Suppose it were, and define the homomorphism
h(a)=h(c)=a,qquadh(b)=h(d)=b.
(11)
Then closure under inverse homomorphism and intersection of a context-free language with a regular language would make
h−1(L)capa+b+c+d+=ambncmdn:m,ngeq1
(12)
context-free. The equality holds because the midpoint of a square with four nonempty alternating runs must lie between its second and third runs.
Apply the pumping lemma for context-free languages to apbpcpdp. A pumpable window of length at most p meets at most two adjacent blocks. Pumping changes at least one block but cannot reach its equal-count partner two blocks away, so either the a,c counts or the b,d counts cease to agree. This contradiction proves the claim.

This language is not context-free. Let p be a proposed pumping length and choose n with 3n≥p. In any pumping decomposition of the unary word a3n, pumping once more increases its length by an integer d with 1≤d≤p. But
3n<3n+d≤2⋅3n<3n+1,
(15)
so the pumped length is not a power of three, contrary to the pumping lemma for context-free languages. This is also an instance of the fact that a unary context-free language is regular, whereas the powers of three are not ultimately periodic.

Yi​∼Poisson(λi​).

In model 1,
logλi​=β0​+βW​Wi​+βE​Ei​+βB​Bi​+βL​Li​+βM​Mi​,

where the variables are indicator variables for winter, weekend, bank holiday, and low or medium pollution; non-winter weekdays that are not bank holidays and have high pollution form the baseline. Model 2 imposes

The models are nested, and the likelihood-ratio test statistic is the decrease in residual deviance,
316.39−304.97=11.42.
(20)
There are three restrictions. By Wilks theorem, under H0​ this statistic is asymptotically a chi-squared distribution with three degrees of freedom. Since
11.42>χ3,0.992​=11.34487,
(21)

r=B−D.

Use the first-order action
S[q,p]=∫t1​t2​​(pq˙​−H(q,p,t))dt.
(33)
Varying q with fixed endpoints and varying p freely gives
δS=∫t1​t2​​[(q˙​−Hp​)δp+(−p˙​−Hq​)δq]dt.
(34)
The principle of stationary action therefore yields Hamilton's equations
q˙​=Hp​,p˙​=−Hq​.
(35)
For H=p2+q−2 these become q˙​=2p and p˙​=2q−3. Along their Hamiltonian flow, H=E is conserved and
dtd​(pq)=p˙​q+pq˙​=2q−2+2p2=2H.
(36)
Thus F=pq−ctH is an integral of motion exactly when c=2.
Write its constant value as F0​. The surfaces pq−2tE=F0​ in extended (q,p,t)-space give
pq=F0​+2Et.
(37)
Using Eq2=p2q2+1,
 q(t)=±E(F0​+2Et)2+1​​,p(t)=q(t)F0​+2Et​ ​.
(38)
The sign of q is fixed. In phase space, each energy orbit is one of the two branches
p2+q−2=E,q=±(E−p2)−1/2,∣p∣<E​.
(39)
Each branch approaches p=−E​ and p=+E​ as ∣q∣→∞ and turns at (p,q)=(0,±E−1/2).

Let H=a′/a=a˙, where a prime denotes differentiation with respect to conformal time dτ=dt/a. Multiplying the Friedmann equation by a2 gives
H2+kc2=38πG​ρa2.
(40)
The critical density is the value obtained when k=0, so
Ω=ρcrit​ρ​=3H28πGρa2​, H2kc2​=Ω−1 ​.
(41)
Since H′=aa¨, the pressure-free Raychaudhuri equation gives
2H′=−38πG​ρa2=−(H2+kc2),
(42)
or
2H′+H2+kc2=0.
(43)
Differentiating Ω=1+kc2/H2 and substituting this equation yields
 Ω′=HΩ(Ω−1) ​.
(44)
For an expanding universe H>0. The Einstein-de Sitter universe Ω=1 is an unstable constant solution: curves starting with 0<Ω<1 decrease towards 0, while curves starting with Ω>1 rise away from 1 and diverge as the closed model reaches maximum expansion. This is the Flatness problem.

b OurBigBook.com
This is superdense coding. To encode 00,01,10,11, Alice applies respectively I,X,Z,XZ to her half of ∣Φ+⟩. These local Pauli operators transform the shared state into the four mutually orthogonal Bell states ∣Φ+⟩,∣Ψ+⟩,∣Φ−⟩,∣Ψ−⟩, up to irrelevant global phases. Alice sends her one qubit to Bob. Bob now holds both qubits and performs a Bell-basis measurement, whose outcome identifies Alice's two-bit message with certainty. One transmitted qubit communicates two classical bits because one shared Bell pair was available beforehand.

(48)
The map (u,v)↦(u,u+v) is injective and linear, so
dim(C1​∣C2​)=dimC1​+dimC2​.
(49)
If di​ is the minimum distance of Ci​, then
wt(u)+wt(u+v)≥wt(v).
(50)
For v=0 this is at least d2​; for v=0 a nonzero word has weight at least 2d1​. Words (0,v) and (u,u) attain these bounds, proving
 d(C1​∣C2​)=min(d2​,2d1​) ​.
(51)
A parity-check matrix P for a code C is a matrix satisfying C=kerP. A pair (x,y) belongs to C1​∣C2​ exactly when
x∈C1​,x+y∈C2​.
(52)
Thus a parity-check matrix is
(P1​P2​​0P2​​)​.

This is the parity-check matrix of a bar product.
The Reed-Muller code RM(d,r) is the length-2d binary code obtained by evaluating every square-free polynomial in d Boolean variables of degree at most r on all points of F2d​. Equivalently,
RM(d,r)=RM(d−1,r)∣RM(d−1,r−1).
(54)
The square-free monomials form a basis, so
 dimRM(d,r)=j=0∑r​(jd​) ​.
(55)
A word in RM(d,1) evaluates an affine function a0​+a⋅x. The two constant functions have weights 0 and 2d. Every nonconstant affine function takes each value equally often, so all other codewords have weight 2d−1.
A monomial of degree j has weight 2d−j. Hence every generator, and therefore every codeword, has even weight when r<d. For r=d, the monomial x1​⋯xd​ has weight one. All words have even weight exactly for 0≤r≤d−1.

Fix an effective enumeration φ0​,φ1​,… of unary partial computable functions. The diagonal halting set is
K={e:φe​(e)↓}.
(56)
It is a computably enumerable set: on input e, simulate φe​(e) and accept if that computation halts.
Suppose K were a computable set. A program could then halt on input e exactly when the decider says e∈/K. Let d be its own index. If d∈K, the program does not halt, while if d∈/K, it halts. Both alternatives contradict the definition of K. Thus K is computably enumerable but not computable.

A many-one reduction A≤m​B is a total computable function f such that
n∈A⟺f(n)∈B.
(57)
If B is a computably enumerable set, compute f(n) and run a semidecision procedure for B on that value. It halts exactly when f(n)∈B, equivalently exactly when n∈A. Therefore A is computably enumerable.

Ordinal exponentiation is defined by transfinite recursion:
α0=1,αβ+1=αβα,αλ=supξ<λ​αξ

when λ is a nonzero limit ordinal. If α≥1, each successor step and each supremum show that β↦αβ is nondecreasing. If α≥2, transfinite induction strengthens this to strict increase: αβ<αβ+1, and the value at a limit exceeds every earlier value.
Strict increase can disappear when the base changes. For example, with ω<ω+1<ω+2,
(ω+1)ω=(ω+2)ω=ωω,
(105)
because for every positive finite n, both finite powers have leading term ωn, and taking the supremum gives ωω.
We next prove

(106)
Apply transfinite induction to γ. The zero and successor cases follow directly from the recursive definitions and the associativity of ordinal multiplication. At a limit λ, continuity of ordinal multiplication in its right argument gives
αβ+λ=supξ<λ​αβ+ξ=supξ<λ​αβαξ=αβαλ.

The superficially similar identity (αβ)γ=αγβγ is false: for α=ω, β=2, and γ=2,
(ω2)2=ω22=ω24=ω222.

 αω1​≥ω1​⟺α≥2 ​, αω1​≥ω2​⟺α≥ω2​ ​.

For the first equivalence, bases zero and one fail, while strict increase embeds every countable ordinal into the powers of any base α≥2. For the second, α≥ω2​ immediately gives αω1​≥α. Conversely, if α<ω2​, then ∣α∣≤ℵ1​. Every exponent below the first uncountable ordinal ω1​ is countable, so each αβ has cardinality at most ℵ1​; the supremum of ℵ1​ such ordinals still has cardinality at most ℵ1​ and is therefore below the second uncountable ordinal ω2​.

Let G be the Galois group of a polynomial of the irreducible quartic. Irreducibility makes G a transitive subgroup of S4​. The three roots of the given cubic resolvent of a quartic correspond to the three partitions of the four quartic roots into two unordered pairs, and the kernel of the S4​-action on these partitions is the Klein four-group V4​. If the resolvent has Galois group S3​, the image of G in this action is all of S3​. Among the transitive subgroups of the symmetric group on four points, only S4​ has this image. Hence
 Gal(f/Q)≅S4​. ​
(121)
Now put fp​(t)=t4+pt+p. The Eisenstein criterion at p proves that fp​ is an irreducible polynomial, and its cubic resolvent is
gp​(t)=t3−4pt−p2.
(122)
Its discriminant of a depressed cubic is
Δp​=256p3−27p4=p3(256−27p).
(123)
For odd p, the p-adic valuation of Δp​ is three because p∤256; for p=2, Δ2​=24⋅101. Thus Δp​ is never a square in Q.
By the rational root theorem, a reducible gp​ has an integer root among ±1,±p,±p2. Reduction modulo p shows that the root is divisible by p; writing it as pk, with k∈{±1,±p}, gives
pk3−4k−1=0.
(124)
The only possibilities are k=−1,p=3 and k=1,p=5, corresponding to roots −3 and 5. For every other prime, gp​ is irreducible with nonsquare discriminant, so its Galois group is S3​ and the criterion above gives the quartic group S4​. For p=3 or 5, the reducible resolvent makes the quartic group a proper subgroup. Therefore
 p=3 or p=5. ​
(125)

The Arzela-Ascoli theorem says that a subset F⊆C(K) is relatively compact in the uniform norm exactly when it is equicontinuous and pointwise bounded.
The real Stone-Weierstrass theorem says that a real subalgebra A⊆C(K,R) is uniformly dense if it contains the constants and separates points of K. In the complex version, a complex subalgebra A⊆C(K,C) must additionally be closed under complex conjugation.
For an example, take K=[0,1] and
F={x↦xn:n≥1}.
(156)
This family is bounded in the uniform norm, but it is not equicontinuous at 1. Equivalently, every subsequence converges pointwise to the discontinuous function that is zero on [0,1) and one at 1, so no subsequence converges uniformly. Thus F is bounded but not relatively compact.

Every compact B⊂Rn lies in some such ball, so the same estimate for all sufficiently large i proves that pi​∣B​→f∣B​ uniformly.

24F OurBigBook.com
A function element is a pair (f,D) consisting of a domain D⊆G and a holomorphic function f:D→C belonging to the given complete analytic function. Its germ of a holomorphic function at z∈D is the equivalence class [f]z​, where two elements are equivalent when they agree on a neighbourhood of z.
For every function element (f,D) and sufficiently small open U⊆D, set
Uf​={[f]z​:z∈U}.
(174)
These sets form a basis for the space of germs of holomorphic functions. The projection
π:G→G,π([f]z​)=z,
(175)
restricts to a homeomorphism Uf​→U. The inverse projections π∣Uf​​ are compatible complex charts, making G a Riemann surface and π a covering map and local biholomorphism. In such a chart, the evaluation map on a space of germs has coordinate expression
E∘(π∣Uf​​)−1(z)=f(z).
(176)
It is therefore holomorphic on every chart, hence analytic on each component of G.
Now let f:R→S be a nonconstant analytic map of compact connected Riemann surfaces, and let B be its finite branch-value set. Each point of B is a branch value of a holomorphic map. At every point of R∖f−1(B) the local degree is one, so the holomorphic inverse-function theorem supplies a neighbourhood on which f is biholomorphic. For y∈S∖B, the fibre is finite. Choose disjoint inverse neighbourhoods around all its points and shrink their common image; compactness, or equivalently properness of f, ensures that no additional preimages enter. Thus
f:R∖f−1(B)⟶S∖B
(177)
is an ordinary unramified covering map.
Fix P∈S∖B. Given a loop γ based at P, lift it from every Q∈f−1(P) and send Q to the endpoint of its lift. The path lifting theorem makes this a permutation; concatenation of loops composes the permutations and reversal gives inverses. Its image is the monodromy group of a covering. The punctured surface R∖f−1(B) is path connected. Given two points of the fibre, join them there by a path; its projection is a loop whose lift joins those points. Hence the monodromy action is transitive.
Finally consider
F(z)=z2+z−2=z2z4+1​.
(178)
It has degree four. Its finite critical points satisfy
F′(z)=2z−2z−3=0,z4=1,
(179)
with branch values 2 and −2; the double poles at zero and infinity give the branch value infinity. For a regular value, the fibre is
{z,−z,z−1,−z−1}.
(180)
The two commuting involutions z↦−z and z↦z−1 preserve F and act transitively on this fibre. They generate all four deck transformations, so the covering is normal and its monodromy group is
 H≅V4​=C2​×C2​. ​
(181)
With the displayed ordering of the fibre, its elements are
1,(12)(34),(13)(24),(14)(23).
(182)
This is the monodromy group of z squared plus z to the minus two.

because x˙=Hy​ and y˙​=−Hx​. The Hessian of H is positive definite at (1,0) and negative definite at (−1,0), so nearby regular level sets are closed curves. Hence both nonhyperbolic equilibria are genuine nonlinear centers.

For a=0 this has a strict constant sign throughout the simply connected plane, so the Bendixson-Dulac criterion proves that there are no periodic orbits. These results comprise the phase portrait of x dot equals two x times y minus a.

In the microcanonical ensemble, the microcanonical energy-shell entropy is the Boltzmann entropy
S(E,V,N;δE)=kB​logΩ(E,V,N;δE).​
(304)
For a macroscopic system, changing the small energy resolution by a fixed factor changes logΩ only by a nonextensive additive term, while S=O(NkB​). Its relative effect therefore vanishes in the thermodynamic limit.
The thermodynamic temperature, pressure, and chemical potential are defined in the entropy representation by
T1​=(∂E∂S​)V,N​,TP​=(∂V∂S​)E,N​,−Tμ​=(∂N∂S​)E,V​.
(305)
Thus
dS=T1​dE+TP​dV−Tμ​dN,
(306)
or, equivalently, the first law of thermodynamics in fundamental form is
dE=TdS−PdV+μdN.​
(307)
